findings.body:
**State when a journal witness is required.**

The unit contract requires a matching journal witness. The default show-only mode explicitly accepts a quiet oneshot with `witness: none` (`UNIT-COMPLETION-DESIGN.md:91–100`). Require the `FragmentPath` match in both modes. State that a matching journal witness is mandatory only in strict mode.
findings.title: State when a journal witness is required.

findings.body:
**Reject terminal unit records with an invalid snapshot identity.**

A `completed` unit record with valid completion entries and `snapshot: null` passes the gate. The classifier checks only that the key exists. The writer requires a dictionary whose `runtime` matches `prior_runtime` (`deploy-controller.py:1939–1941`).

Apply that same structural check in the classifier. Valid terminal history should still clear the gate. Malformed history should name the record and refuse the next operation.
findings.title: Reject terminal unit records with an invalid snapshot identity.

findings.body:
**Rebaseline after a prior restore may have activated the unit.**

If `install()` fails in `drained`, the rollback path can restore prior activation and then stop before it records `rolled_back`. The durable record has `phase: restore_activation_pending` and `failed_phase: drained` (`deploy-controller.py:1983–1991`). If the prior runtime completes a tick before the retry, `recover` uses the older `failed_phase` and compares against stale queue and heartbeat digests. It fails preservation even when the new restore leaves both files unchanged.

Use the current phase as well as the original failed phase to decide whether to rebaseline after the fence. Keep the original failed phase for diagnosis. Keep the original baseline when neither phase permitted activation.
findings.title: Rebaseline after a prior restore may have activated the unit.

findings.body:
**Make snapshot-phase intents recoverable through the CLI.**

The controller writes `state: null` before `stop_and_drain()` (`deploy-controller.py:1945–1948`). If the process stops after the adapter stops an activator, `recover` accepts the pending record but cannot derive `source_sha`. It refuses before it can restore the activator, and the intent continues to block other controller operations.

Capture and validate the prior render source before writing the snapshot-phase intent. Store it separately from the post-drain preservation baseline. Use the retained source in both snapshot-phase and later recovery; do not fall back to the current `HEAD`.
findings.title: Make snapshot-phase intents recoverable through the CLI.

findings.body:
**Document the retained source SHA used for recovery.**

The guide says that advancing `HEAD` changes the composed selection. The controller instead passes `source_sha` from the retained `state.prior_head` (`deploy-controller.py:1597–1602`, `deploy-controller.py:2303–2305`). Show that argument in the example. Distinguish the pinned source used to compose the adapter from the snapshot used to restore bytes and activation.
findings.title: Document the retained source SHA used for recovery.

findings.body:
**Use the health failure exit code for heartbeat read errors.**

If the heartbeat exists but cannot be read, `read_completion_heartbeat()` converts the I/O error to `Refused` (`deploy-controller.py:291–297`). The CLI exits 2. An I/O error that escapes a later health observation exits 1, as the health handler promises.

Translate heartbeat observation failures to exit 1 at the health boundary. Preserve exit 2 for checkout and unit refusals, and keep one JSON artifact in both cases. As per coding guidelines, “Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 thrown error, 2 arg error, 3 needs-human.”
findings.title: Use the health failure exit code for heartbeat read errors.

findings.body:
**Handle record-path refusals inside the JSON error boundary.**

On Python 3.12, a symlink loop in the parent of `--record-dir` makes `Path.resolve()` raise `RuntimeError`. `absolute_record_dir()` translates it to `Refused`, but this call occurs before the handler. With `--json`, the CLI emits a traceback on stderr and no JSON. Move path setup into the guarded block so this refusal follows the existing JSON path. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/pathlib.html?highlight=pathlib&utm_source=openai))

As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.”
findings.title: Handle record-path refusals inside the JSON error boundary.

findings.body:
**Hold the queue-dispatch exclusion through activation.**

`switch_unit` drains the publisher with `stop_and_drain` at `deploy-controller.py:1948`. That call fences only the selected unit and its activators. It does not stop `crq-tick.service`. The last queue observation is at `ops/unit-adapter.py:1483`. The unit switch then installs the new unit and runs `preservation_check` at `deploy-controller.py:1956`. The controller takes only `controller.lock`, and nothing in `deploy-controller.py` takes `tick.lock`. The tick runner holds `tick.lock` only for its own run. A tick can therefore start queue work after the last observation and before activation. This violates the fence contract stated in the `switch_unit` docstring: the stop/drain fence "must prevent new work until start."

Choose one mechanism that excludes tick dispatch from the drain observation through activation. Either hold `tick.lock` across the transaction, or fence `crq-tick.service` for that interval. The required behavior is exclusion of new queue work through `deploy-controller.py:1956`.
findings.title: Hold the queue-dispatch exclusion through activation.

findings.body:
**Keep admission held when drain diagnostics cannot be written.**

If the queue drain expires with live work and writing `drain.json` fails, the I/O error replaces `FailStop`. If the work has not yet changed the measured bytes, pre-switch recovery can restart the triggers and release admission. Preserve `FailStop` even if the diagnostic write fails. A successful drain can still follow the normal recording path.
findings.title: Keep admission held when drain diagnostics cannot be written.

findings.body:
**Check unfinished controller transactions before claiming admission.**

An unresolved journal does not stop this runbook from claiming the hold and stopping triggers. If a service fails to drain, the runbook keeps its own hold and never reaches the journal check. Move the first journal check to after the controller lock is acquired and before `Hold.acquire()`. A clear journal still permits the normal drain and switch.
findings.title: Check unfinished controller transactions before claiming admission.

findings.body:
**Report a retained rollback hold in the recovery record.**

If health fails, rollback can reacquire admission and then fail before releasing it. The recovery record still says `released: true` because that value describes the earlier health window. Record current admission separately from whether the health window opened. Keep the historical value for choosing the rollback digest baseline.
findings.title: Report a retained rollback hold in the recovery record.

findings.body:
**Require hold ownership before restarting triggers during recovery.**

If an operator replaces this run’s marker with a manual hold after the triggers stop, `acquired` remains true. Recovery can start the triggers, skip release when `owns()` returns false, and exit 2 as if it restored the host. Check ownership before starting triggers and require `Hold.release()` to succeed. Lost ownership must go to recovery-required without removing the operator’s marker.






Also applies to: 1197-1198
findings.title: Require hold ownership before restarting triggers during recovery.

findings.body:
**Block admission release when post-switch compatibility fails.**

If the compatibility check returns a negative record after the digest check passes, this branch only sets `rollback_disabled`. Nothing reads it. The runbook releases admission and starts the target triggers without the required rollback evidence. Raise a refusal here while the hold is still owned. Recovery can then apply its compatibility checks without first admitting work on the target.
findings.title: Block admission release when post-switch compatibility fails.

findings.body:
**Persist the post-drain digests before switching.**

If a tick finishes during the drain, the recovery receipt contains the old queue and heartbeat digests. `recheck_baseline()` updates the live baseline but writes only its keys. If the process dies during the switch, the operator cannot verify whether the switch preserved the bytes that were actually present when it began. Keep the pre-admission receipt and write a separate durable checkpoint with the full post-drain digests before calling the helper.
findings.title: Persist the post-drain digests before switching.

findings.body:
**Do not direct the operator to a step that leaves the deploy blocked.**

Installing the target unit files does not change either Git tree. A retry still finds the same template delta and refuses. State that this runbook cannot deploy a template-changing target from the current checkout, and point to the separate operator procedure if one exists.
findings.title: Do not direct the operator to a step that leaves the deploy blocked.

findings.body:
**Re-read the rollback permission in `complete()` before recording it.**

`complete()` sets `permitted: True` without reading the queue. Health checks do not read the queue either, so a healthy tick can coexist with a queue that has a schema marker. The record then reports rollback as permitted after the queue state has changed. Read the compatibility record in `complete()` and derive `permitted` from it:

```diff
     def complete(self):
+        compatibility = self.controller.compatibility_record(self.effects, self.prior_sha)
         self.rollback = {
-            "permitted": True,
+            "permitted": self.controller.rollback_compatible(compatibility),
             "to": self.prior_sha,
             "cq_bin": self.cq_bin,
             "statement": "rollback is available while the queue carries no "
                          "schema marker or author_* keys; this run invoked it "
                          "only on failure",
         }
```
findings.title: Re-read the rollback permission in `complete()` before recording it.

findings.body:
**Check the rollback target before admission. A local prior SHA passes preflight but cannot be rolled back to.**

`_run` checks only that the live `HEAD` is a full SHA. Only the target is tested for merged-main ancestry. The prior SHA therefore reaches the queue-shape check and the switch with no ancestry test (`apps/crq-python/ops/deploy-runbook.py:675-676`, `:713-718`). Rollback then calls `helper.switch(..., self.prior_sha, None)` (`:1060-1061`). That call runs `verify_target` on the prior SHA. The check requires the SHA to be an ancestor of `refs/remotes/origin/main` and of `POLICY_FLOOR` (`apps/crq-python/ops/prepare-host.py:742-743`, `:763-765`). A prior SHA that is not merged to `origin/main` fails there, after the forward switch has installed the target. Recovery then keeps admission held and raises recovery required (`deploy-runbook.py:1231-1233`, `:1250-1252`). The triggers stopped at `:1033` restart only after a successful rollback switch (`:1081`).

Refuse the deploy before admission and before any switch when the prior SHA would fail the helper's `verify_target` rollback check. The preflight and rollback then apply the same rule.
findings.title: Check the rollback target before admission. A local prior SHA passes preflight but cannot be rolled back to.
